info.title: AE REST API documentation
info.description:
The AE REST API provides an interface for 3rd party applications to interact with the Automation Engine. It allows you to target the AE from many programming languages, not only from Java. The AE REST API will eventually expose the most important AE API features for 3rd party developers.

Please see the AE Java API if you are looking for a more comprehensive API.

The URI for each request has the form http[s]://{host}:{port}/ae/api/{version}.

  • host: required (string)The host (IP address or hostname) on which the REST is running
  • port: required (string)Port of the REST as configured in the REST section of ucsrv.ini (by default the port is set to 8088)
  • version: required (string)API version, must be v1

Note: If a parameter in the URI contains special characters, it needs to be encoded by replacing each of them with '%' followed by the two hexadecimal digits representing the ASCII code of that character.
Example: The character '/' is encoded as '%2F'.

Responses which contain HTTP Status Codes 4xx through 5xx signal client / server errors. Details are delivered in the response body, formatted as application/json. Depending on the number of errors, the top level element of responses will either be an array of or a single object of type OutError or OutValidationError. Please see POST /{client_id}/executions [400] and [401] for an example.

A health check is available under GET /{client_id}/health. Be aware that solely the HTTP status code should be used to determine the health ([200] signals healthy, [503] not healthy). A response body is optionally delivered, depending on whether a PWP is currently present or not. If no PWP is present, a body of type OutError is returned, otherwise it will be of type OutHealthCheck.

Basic Authentication is used to authenticate users in the system, so make sure the Authorization header is present for each request. The user-pass section can be entered in the following 3 formats USERNAME:PASSWORD, USERNAME/DEPARTMENT:PASSWORD and CLIENT/USERNAME/DEPARTMENT:PASSWORD. The character encoding scheme used to convert this section into an octet sequence is expected to be ISO-8859-1.

The internal authorization system is used to authorize inbound requests. Depending on the endpoint, different privileges and authorizations are needed. If missing, a [403] with details will be returned.

Some resources may be disabled till a given precondition is met eg. a mandatory configuration parameter is set. A call to a disabled resource yields a [404] with a custom error code and message.

post.summary: Search the process assembly for objects using different filter criteria.
post.description:
Note: In order to search for objects, you need to define at least one filter object (see below) and append it to the filter array of the JSON payload. An object has to match every filter of your search to be included in the result set.

Note: The search will consider the folder permissions of the AWI user who executed the API request - it will not find objects that are inaccessible for this user. However, it does not consider permissions directly configured in an object. Therefore you should use defensive programming when processing the search results - i.e. your code must be able to handle access violation errors.

Note: To sort the result set you can populate property sort_columns. This example shows how to sort the result set after name ascending and title descending. Following properties are supported: name, type, sub_type, platform, title, archive_key1, archive_key2, folder_path, modified_date, last_used_date, creation_date, calendar_event_name, calendar_event_ctype, calendar_event_valid_from, calendar_event_valid_to.

post.summary: Performs an action in the Zero Downtime Upgrade Process.
post.description:
This operation can only be executed in client 0.

	The following actions are available during the Zero Downtime Upgrade (ZDU) process:

	- BEGIN: Activates ZDU, allowing the user to run DBLOAD even while processes are running.
	- CHECKDB: Checks whether a higher AE version exists in the UC_ZDU database table.
	- CHECK_PROCESSES: Verifies that the processes from the target AE version are up and running.
	- UPGRADE: Switches the PWP role to the target AE version and makes the new MQSET active.
	- ROLLBACK: Keeps the PWP role on the target AE version but switches the active MQSET back to the base version.
	- CHECK_CONNECTIONS: Verifies whether any users or agents are still connected to a non-active MQSET (base version).
	- CHECK_EXECUTIONS: Checks for any active activities in the base version.
	- CLEANUP_EXECUTIONS: Ends all active activities in the base version with the status "Inconsistent" and adds a comment.
	- FINALIZE: Shuts down all processes from the base AE version and sets the target version as ACTIVE and BASE in UC_ZDU table.
	- FINALIZE_ROLLBACK: Shuts down all processes from the target AE version and assigns the PWP role back to the base AE version.
	- END: Used only by the UI to close the ZDU Wizard.
